note: Intra-actor RayX/HPX native CPU scaling inside one long-lived Ray actor, validated on a homogeneous 40-core Linux Xeon node. Clean through W=16; W=32 is a lower-efficiency, placement-sensitive region (bimodal across fresh invocations), not a smooth knee and not a straggler explosion. Per-leg normalized; engine-clean view is the in-actor wall. Not a Ray comparison, performance, sizing, or capacity claim. No socket/NUMA attribution without binding/affinity evidence.
raw_logs: kept outside the tracked tree under the ignored results/ (e.g. results/exp32_rostam_40core_tail/)

decouple.resolves: the prior Mac/laptop decouple INCONCLUSIVE result, for the homogeneous Linux case

interpretation.W16: Clean, near-linear, replicated 3/3; efficiency approx 0.89-0.90; tail-diagnostic spread approx 1-2%. The load-bearing Linux result. Python flat.
interpretation.W32: Lower-efficiency, placement-sensitive region. Median speedup still improves to approx 17-18x but efficiency drops to approx 0.53-0.56. Within-run spread bounded approx 27-31% (10-rep tail diagnostic); the 756.7%/910% reps=5 figures are outlier-sensitive low-rep artifacts, superseded. Distribution is bimodal (fast approx 4.6-4.7 ms, slow approx 6.0-6.2 ms) and the dominant mode flips between fresh Runtime/Ray-actor invocations, so the variation is mostly between invocations, not a within-run straggler tail. Not a smooth knee and not a catastrophic straggler explosion.
interpretation.numa_socket: Hypothesis only. W=32 exceeds the 20-core-per-socket boundary on this 2-socket node, so a socket/NUMA explanation is plausible and consistent with the between-invocation bimodality, but it is NOT attributed without binding/affinity/numactl evidence.
interpretation.exp34: Do not start exp34. It is less blocked now (W=32 is bounded and characterized, not chaos) but remains a separate decision. W<=16 is the clean regime for a latency/mix experiment; if exp34 uses W=32 it must treat W=32 as a lower-efficiency, placement-sensitive regime.

claims_allowed: On a homogeneous 40-core Linux Xeon node, exp32 validates intra-actor RayX/HPX native CPU scaling cleanly through W=16.
The decoupling panel supports the expected min(num_lanes, hpx_threads, cores) bound.
W=32 still improves median speedup but enters a lower-efficiency, placement-sensitive region.
claims_forbidden: raw Python-vs-RayX wall-time speedup as the point
